classification.difficultyReason: Explain the hour-hand displacement at half past and calculate the resulting nonzero separation.

inlines.text: Benji thinks that the angle between the hands of a clock at 6:30 pm is
Explain why Benji is wrong and find the correct angle.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11, clock below the stem at the left
spec.description: Unshaded circular clock with a heavy black rim, 60 minute ticks, conventional hour numerals, a central pivot, a longer minute hand pointing to 6 and a shorter hour hand halfway between 6 and 7. No angle arc or angle label.
spec.mathematics: Hand directions measured clockwise from 12 are 180 degrees and 195 degrees. All twelve numerals are complete 10 pt labels; the hands have visibly different lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: The source clock is part of the student question. The 15-degree answer is not labelled.
spec.shadingDecision: White face with structural black pivot and arrowheads; no shaded mathematical region.

answer.short: The hour hand has moved halfway from 6 to 7, so the angle is $15^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The hour hand is not at 6 when it is 6:30; it is halfway between 6 and 7. The minute hand points to 6. The hands are $\frac{1}{24}$ of a revolution apart.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Angle} &= \frac{360^\circ}{24}\\\text{Angle} &= 15^\circ\end{align*}$$
